doc.texto:
1. The explainability gap is the real problem.
2. What the real problem is, is the explainability gap.

abertura: Mark the three statements that are true.

itens.t: They contain the same information.
The second one tells the listener that a conclusion is arriving.
The second one is more formal.
The second one puts the new information at the end.
The first one is wrong.
Only the second one can be used in a presentation.

sec1.rationale: Neither is wrong. English puts what is new at the END of the sentence, and these three structures exist to move it there — which is why they sound like signalling even though they are only word order.

nota.titulo: This is the grammar under lesson 3
nota.texto: What this means is… is not an expression you memorize. It is a structure — and once you have it, you can build it around anything: what we found was…, what worries me is…, what nobody has asked is…

abertura: Choose the better reading for each structure.

itens.t: What we found was a gap in the logs.
alts: I am announcing that the finding is coming
I am not sure what we found
itens.ok: I am announcing that the finding is coming

itens.t: As for the budget, that is a separate conversation.
alts: the budget is the main subject
I am picking one topic out of several and parking it
itens.ok: I am picking one topic out of several and parking it

itens.t: While the accuracy is there, the explainability is not.
alts: the two happen at the same time
I am conceding one thing to make the other land
itens.ok: I am conceding one thing to make the other land

itens.t: It is the timing that worries me, not the design.
alts: I am correcting what you assumed
I am worried about everything
itens.ok: I am correcting what you assumed

itens.t: What I am asking for is six weeks.
alts: I am asking a question
I am making the ask, and it lands at the end
itens.ok: I am making the ask, and it lands at the end

itens.t: While I take that point, it does not change the date.
alts: I am conceding without moving
I agree and I am changing my mind

nota.titulo: Why these three and not others
nota.texto: They are the three that do the work of a discourse marker with word order alone. You already have the markers from lesson 3; these are what let you build your own instead of reaching for the six you memorized.

abertura: Six sentences. Which of the three structures is each one using?

itens.t: "What surprised the team was the false-decline rate."
"As for October, that date was never mine."
"While the pilot succeeded, it did not test this."
"What we cannot do is explain a single decision."
"While I understand the pressure, six weeks is six weeks."
"As for the engineering cost, I have the number."

nota.titulo: The concessive is the one that changes the room
nota.texto: A cleft makes you clear. Fronting makes you organized. The concessive makes you credible — it is the sentence that proves you already considered the objection, and it is the one most people leave out.

abertura: Each sentence is neutral. Rebuild it so the new information lands at the end.

itens.t: The false-decline rate surprised the team.
alts: The team was surprised by the false-decline rate.
What surprised the team was the false-decline rate.
Surprisingly, the false-decline rate was high.
itens.ok: What surprised the team was the false-decline rate.

itens.t: I am asking for six weeks.
alts: I would like six weeks.
Six weeks is my ask.
What I am asking for is six weeks.
itens.ok: What I am asking for is six weeks.

itens.t: The budget is a different discussion.
alts: As for the budget, that is a different discussion.
The budget discussion is different.
There is another discussion about the budget.
itens.ok: As for the budget, that is a different discussion.

itens.t: The accuracy is good but the model cannot explain itself.
alts: The model cannot explain itself, but the accuracy is good.
While the accuracy is there, the model cannot explain itself.
The accuracy is good and the model cannot explain itself.
itens.ok: While the accuracy is there, the model cannot explain itself.

itens.t: I am worried about the timing, not the design.
alts: I have a worry about the timing.
It is the timing that worries me, not the design.
The timing worries me more than the design.
itens.ok: It is the timing that worries me, not the design.

nota.titulo: The rejected options are not wrong
nota.texto: Every alternative here is correct English. They just leave the new information in the middle, where the listener has already stopped waiting for it. In writing that is harmless; out loud, in a room, it is the difference between being followed and being read back.

abertura: Complete each sentence with the right form. No word bank — the point is the structure, not the word.
itens: What the board {wants|110px} is a date they can hold us to.
It {is|70px} the explainability that fails, not the accuracy.
{While|90px} I take the point about cost, the number does not move.
What we {are|80px} not able to do is explain a single decline.
As {for|70px} the October date, it was never a commitment.
{What|90px} worries me most is the gap between the two markets.

nota.texto: What the board wants is — the verb agrees with the whole clause, not with board. And It is the explainability that fails — the it is is fixed; it does not become they are even when what follows is plural.

abertura: Write six sentences about a decision you are carrying right now — two of each structure. Bring them to the lesson; they are what you will say out loud.

dg5.prompt: Which of these did she actually say? Mark the two.

itens.t: What we cannot do is explain a single decision.
We cannot explain a single decision.
While the accuracy is there, the explainability is not.
The accuracy is there but the explainability is not.
Explainability is missing, accuracy is fine.

dg5.rationale: All five say the same thing and two of them are the ones a room remembers. The difference is where the new information sits, and it is the only difference.

itens.t: "What this means is that we would ship blind."
"As for the marketing date, that is not mine to move."
"While I take the cost point, six weeks is six weeks."
"What worries me is not the model, it is the timing."
"As for who asked first, I will send that today."
"While the pilot was clean, it did not test this."

nota.texto: As for X, … lets you take a topic out of the argument without refusing to discuss it. In a room with eleven minutes, that is the difference between staying on your point and being pulled onto somebody else's.

abertura: A quick reference to the three structures.

tabela: What we found was… · What I am asking for is… · It is the timing that worries me.
Announces that a conclusion or an ask is arriving, and lands it at the end.
Takes one topic out of several and parks it, without refusing it.
While the accuracy is there, … · While I take that point, …
Concedes something real and holds the position anyway. It is what makes the rest credible.

abertura: Record a short voice message, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
Take the six sentences you wrote for activity 6.

What you are trying to do: say them out loud, in one minute, as if they were part of an argument — not as six separate sentences.

abertura: Take any paragraph you wrote in English this month — an email, a summary, a note — and rewrite two sentences of it with the new information at the end.

callout.texto: The structures are easy to produce in an exercise and hard to produce in your own writing, where the Portuguese order is already on the page. Rewriting is where they transfer.

abertura: Short and precise, on the thing this lesson is about.

itens.texto: The reference for what.. is.. and it is.. that.., with examples and audio. It is the same structure you used today.

abertura: One talk, watched for one thing.

itens.titulo: The danger of a single story
itens.texto: Watch for the concessives. She concedes something to the other side roughly every two minutes, and it is why an argument that could sound accusatory does not.

abertura: The sentences were written for this lesson, in the situation of lessons 3 and 4. The Cambridge entry is the public grammar reference.
